candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records , and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records , and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

evidence_packet.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Retail units along the stretch are expected to be demolished to create room New pedestrian routes would then connect to the square, running along Minden Parade and Market Parade. For this, parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre’s roof would be demolished along with a portion of the B&M store by the multi-storey car park

candidates.evidence_text: Jewish Communities The programme designed to tackle anti-semitism in our Greater Manchester schools "It's a powerful message to hear that from someone who survived the Holocaust" Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:42, 10 No A new teaching resource aimed at tackling antisemitism in schools across Greater Manchester has been launched. The Fed's My Voice Project is an educational initiative which features over 50 authentic, captivating tales of Holocaust survival in the survivors' own words The project is run by Jewish social care charity The Fed. The initiative was officially launched at the Star Radcliffe Academy on Thursday (November 5) Councillors and school chiefs attended the event, which featured a moving speech by Holocaust survivor Anne Super, who recalled her days as a Jewish orphan hiding from German officers The project provides four ready-to-use lesson plans for secondary school teachers. Schools can sign up by registering with the Fed's My Voice Project The project will also offer long term support and monitoring of the scheme. Also in attendance of the launch was Deputy Mayor of Greater Manchester Kate Green, who also delivered a speech

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Work starts to remove 18,000 tonne ‘ocean’ of toxic waste at illegal dump in Wigan The £4.8M project is set to clear the site by spring, 2027 Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:40, 10 Nov 2026 View Image Work will start today to clear the huge Bickershaw illegal waste site, the government has announced. The ‘ocean of rubbish’ piled up during the early months of 2025 and is expected cost around £4.8m to clean-up In September, Wigan council said contractor Acumen Waste Services Ltd will clean up the huge piles of rubbish at the site close to Bolton House Road Around 18,000 tonnes of toxic waste were illegally placed there In July, 2025 a week-long fire saw tonnes of waste burned, emitting dangerous fumes and forcing nearby schools to close. The dump is within Andy Burnham ’s Makerfield constituency The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) said the clean up move would ‘bring relief to a community that has endured major disruption from the notorious site’

The council said it is ‘aware of the damage’ and is determining what course of action Bosses have also referred the matter to police Airing their anger on social media, one parent wrote: “The kids in this area are beyond nasty and unappreciative. That park was done so nicely and they destroyed everything. I don’t know why and how would anyone think of doing something like that.” View 3 Images Safety fencing around the burnt-out swing. Many areas are decrepit after 121 years treating patients Stepping Hill, which first opened in 1905, employs around 6,300 staff and sees over 91,000 patient admissions in a year. It is run by Stockport NHS Foundation Trust One medic says wards are ‘falling apart’, claiming some buildings ‘need to be condemned’. Patients sometimes have to be transferred elsewhere or have surgeries cancelled, they add, with the ‘snowball effect’ making waiting times worse Pictures inside show disintegrating walls; leaking roofs; and precarious floors. candidates.lead: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopp
candidates.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Retail units along the stretch are expected to be demolished to create room New pedestrian routes would then connect to the square, running along Minden Parade and Market Parade. For this, parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre’s roof would be demolished along with a portion of the B&M store by the multi-storey car park

candidates.evidence_text: Jewish Communities The programme designed to tackle anti-semitism in our Greater Manchester schools "It's a powerful message to hear that from someone who survived the Holocaust" Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 06:42, 10 No A new teaching resource aimed at tackling antisemitism in schools across Greater Manchester has been launched. The Fed's My Voice Project is an educational initiative which features over 50 authentic, captivating tales of Holocaust survival in the survivors' own words The project is run by Jewish social care charity The Fed. The initiative was officially launched at the Star Radcliffe Academy on Thursday (November 5) Councillors and school chiefs attended the event, which featured a moving speech by Holocaust survivor Anne Super, who recalled her days as a Jewish orphan hiding from German officers The project provides four ready-to-use lesson plans for secondary school teachers. Schools can sign up by registering with the Fed's My Voice Project The project will also offer long term support and monitoring of the scheme. Also in attendance of the launch was Deputy Mayor of Greater Manchester Kate Green, who also delivered a speech

candidates.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Retail units along the stretch are expected to be demolished to create room New pedestrian routes would then connect to the square, running along Minden Parade and Market Parade. For this, parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre’s roof would be demolished along with a portion of the B&M store by the multi-storey car park

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig makes demand to Northern to put Greater Manchester Sunday trains 'at the top of the list' Mayor Craig will also be meeting with Northern to discuss a rollout plan Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News re Bev Craig says the region must be the first in line for the return of the full Sunday timetable on the railway. The Mayor of Greater Manchester's demand comes after Northern and RMT union agreed a deal to run more Sunday trains after years of a reduced timetable A long-running dispute between the operator and union regarding conductors has seen a third of timetabled Sunday trains cancelled in Greater Manchester over the last two years. candidates.evidence_text: Etihad Stadium Manchester City will pay extra £320k a year to the council in new Etihad Campus lease deal The town hall has shared details of its new arrangement with the Blues Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Report Manchester City will pay an extra £320,000 a year to the council for its lease at the Etihad Campus as part of an updated agreement Town hall papers published in August revealed a variation to the lease in light of the changes taking place to the stadium and surrounding land, which has been transformed into a major visitor destination since the ground first opened for the 2002 Commonwealth Games New figures released by the council have revealed it will pocket extra each year from its leases with the football club, with a further £33,000 for the stadium lease, £252,000 for City Square, and £35,680 from land in the new Medlock Square hotel and entertainment zone The extra cash will add to the total amount paid to the council by City, which stood at £6.3m last year, made up of £4.4m in rent, £1.1m from naming rights, and £790,000 from income from Champions League games Lease payments for the stadium and City Square are set to increase in future through inflation-linked increases, while the land lease at Medlock Square includes an annual rent uplift of three per cent and future reviews

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

candidates.evidence_text: Russell LDP and JAG Woodford's plans for Woodford Garden Village include a grand total of 567 homes. Credit: via planning documents Councillors sided with officers on all four major applications on the planning committee’s agenda on Thursday, which was good news for Story Homes, Russell, and Bellway – and not so great for Barratt and David Wilson Homes Woodford Garden Village underwent a series of changes from its original proposals, with councillors ultimately voting in favour of the building of up to 423 homes, up to 72 fully affordable extra care apartments, and a 72-bed care home on a 75-acre site off Chester Road The plans also include 1,100 sq ft of retail space, a 6,500 sq ft health centre, and a 6,500 sq ft day nursery with outdoor space. There would also be a mobility point with cycle parking, parcel lockers, and a bus stop Russell’s plans include a 16-acre nature park that could hold nature trails, allotments, an orchard, and children’s play area. This, combined with open space allocated around the site, leads to ta total open space provision of 24.7 acres Looking at the housing plans, up to 248 homes would be affordable. This includes the 72 extra care apartments. Of those 248 homes, 22% are envisioned as social rent, 13% for affordable rent, and 65% for affordable ownership

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Carrington Relief Road is seen as crucial to unlocking land for millions of sq ft of employment space. Credit: via Trafford Council Trafford Council voted seven to six to approve its own proposals for the 2.7-mile carriageway, which has been hailed as a crucial bit of infrastructure to enable the delivery of 5,000 homes and 3.8m sq ft of employment space The Carrington Relief Road has been part of Trafford Council’s development plans since 1996. Spanning a 115-acre stretch between the A6144 Manchester and in Carrington and the A6144 Carrington Lane/Carrington Spur in Sale, the road is estimated to cost £130m to build Helping the numbers stack up, Greater Manchester Combined Authority has awarded the project £89.1m from its Good Growth Fund . Additional support is expected to come from Section 106 agreements with developers. Two such agreements have been part of appeals and court cases Alongside the road itself, there will be a 2.5-metre-wide cycle lane a 2.5-metre-wide footpath on either side, encouraging active travel As part of the proposals, 25 acres of open grassland is proposed to help provide habitats for skylarks and other animals. Helping with biodiversity will be the planting of trees to make up for those felled during the construction of the road, as well as miles of hedgerows. Sustai

evidence_texts: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004

The noise sounded great, but we didn't see a thing." Freelance photographer Tanya Weekes also attended Platt Fields Park on Saturday and said the fog made looking at the fireworks "a bit scary" "It was a strange feeling, just staring into the mist and fog [with] very loud music playing." She added families took to arranging their own entertainment, forming a conga line to dance to the music in the absence of anything to watch Listen to the best of BBC Radio Manchester on Sounds and follow BBC Manchester on Facebook , X , and Instagram . evidence_packet.title: Major boost for Middleton as sale of landmark town centre building completes - Rochdale Borough Council
evidence_packet.lead: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developers, Kam Lei Fong
evidence_packet.summary: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developers, Kam Lei Fong
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton’s regeneration has taken another major step forward with the council formally completing the purchase of Warwick Mill from developers, Kam Lei Fong Once a thriving cotton mill, the imposing structure, which was built in 1907, has been vacant for at least a decade and has since become an eyesore, regularly attracting vandalism and urban explorers The council sees redevelopment of Warwick Mill, which is Grade II listed, as a major opportunity to bring an important historic building back into use as new homes for the benefit of the Middleton community The neighbouring 1960s office block, London House, has also been purchased as part of the £3.3 million deal, with plans to demolish the building Work to transform the building will get under way quickly. Rochdale firm, Winterburns, is set to take over security immediately, with a beefed up, 24-hour presence on site. The firm will also start clearing the mountain of debris which has built up over years of neglect, includin Teams will soon start the delicate internal strip out of Warwick Mill and London House. The demolition of London House, a brutalist structure with little architectural merit, is set to get under way early in the New Year

candidates.evidence_text: Pupils across Bolton returning from the summer holidays last month were greeted by safer and warmer classrooms after the council invested in the borough’s schools Working with local employers Seddon, the council oversaw repairs and improvements at more than half a dozen schools, benefitting over 3,000 pupils from primary to secondary age The wide-ranging work was carried out over the summer break to minimise disruption The project saw some schools receiving new boilers and water heaters, new roof installed at one primary school, while another had more energy efficient windows installed Some fire alarm systems and emergency lighting have also been upgraded It is the second school decarbonisation project Seddon has delivered with Bolton Council, helping to improve the efficiency and long-term sustainability of school buildings across the borough

Through a process of reflection and catharsis the sculptures were created in carefully devised, movement informed workshops with individuals who have experience of grief. Made using tr The central space is immersed in sanguine red. Produced and performed in private, the enigmatic forms are instinctual. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: IMAGINE at First Street - Manchester’s Finest IMAGINE at First Street Thu 12th Nov, 2026 - Tony Wilson Place IMAGINE at First Street Tony Wilson Place, sold, First St, Manchester M15 4GU Thu 12th Nov, 2026 Free Directions events Go to Manchester's Finest Facebook page Go to Manchester's Finest X profile First Street are helping you bring your imagination to life this winter as they welcome a giant screen that gives visitors the chance to see themselves transformed into animals, mythical beings and beyond. Using AI and body tracking technology, visitors can step in front of the screen and see an entirely new creature mirrored in front of them. Dance, jump and play as a giant gingerbread monster, an alien in a Santa hat or something else all together. The AI-powered screen, created by Manchester studio SUPERMASSIVE, will be free to interact with, landing at First Street from 6pm on 12 November and available to interact with throughout the Christmas period. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

candidates.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . candidates.evidence_text: Pasture, the restaurant group celebrated for its open-fire cooking, provenance and sustainability, is set to arrive in Manchester thanks to a new partnership with Relentless Developments and Salboy at St Michael’s Pasture will operate four distinct destinations within St Michael’s: Pasture Manchester, a flagship ground-floor restaurant within the scheme’s 43-storey tower; W Lounge, the hotel bar situated in W Hotel Manchester; Abercromby, the treasured historic pub being sensitively restor Together, the four venues will create a varied food and drink experience at the heart of one of Manchester’s most ambitious new developments, complementing the existing iconic hospitality brands already open at No.1 St Michael’s Founded in 2018 by chef-owner, Sam Elliott, Pasture has grown from its original Bristol restaurant to a number of established restaurants and bars across Bristol, Cardiff and Birmingham. The group’s approach centres on cooking over fire, carefully-sourced ingredients, expertly-pr Sam Elliott, Chef-Owner of Pasture, commented: “Manchester is a city with a huge personality, a strong independent spirit and a real passion for great food, so bringing Pasture here is incredibly exciting. St Michael’s gives us the opportunity to create something that goes beyond “From our signature open-fire cooking at Pasture Manchester and Mediterranean-inspired all-day dining at Terrace, to the atmosphere of W Lounge and the much-loved character of the Abercromby, we’re looking forward to becoming part of the city’s dynamic hospitality scene.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Pasture, the restaurant group celebrated for its open-fire cooking, provenance and sustainability, is set to arrive in Manchester thanks to a new partnership with Relentless Developments and Salboy at St Michael’s Pasture will operate four distinct destinations within St Michael’s: Pasture Manchester, a flagship ground-floor restaurant within the scheme’s 43-storey tower; W Lounge, the hotel bar situated in W Hotel Manchester; Abercromby, the treasured historic pub being sensitively restor Together, the four venues will create a varied food and drink experience at the heart of one of Manchester’s most ambitious new developments, complementing the existing iconic hospitality brands already open at No.1 St Michael’s Founded in 2018 by chef-owner, Sam Elliott, Pasture has grown from its original Bristol restaurant to a number of established restaurants and bars across Bristol, Cardiff and Birmingham. The group’s approach centres on cooking over fire, carefully-sourced ingredients, expertly-pr Sam Elliott, Chef-Owner of Pasture, commented: “Manchester is a city with a huge personality, a strong independent spirit and a real passion for great food, so bringing Pasture here is incredibly exciting. St Michael’s gives us the opportunity to create something that goes beyond “From our signature open-fire cooking at Pasture Manchester and Mediterranean-inspired all-day dining at Terrace, to the atmosphere of W Lounge and the much-loved character of the Abercromby, we’re looking forward to becoming part of the city’s dynamic hospitality scene.”

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Manchester Digital Festival 2027: Programme revealed as tickets go on sale
candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Researchers argue that universities need to move beyond treating AI primarily as a technical challenge or a threat to academic integrity, and develop a better understanding of how students and staff engage with it. The research examined how academic staff and students perceived their own use of generative AI tools, as well as their views of how the technology was being used in higher education. The study surveyed 45 academic staff and 86 students in a school covering social science disciplines at a UK research-intensive university. The questionnaires were conducted between April and June 2024, so essentially before AI took over the likes of Google whether you asked it to or not. When asked about students’ use of AI for academic purposes, staff gave an average rating of 5.23 on a seven-point scale. Students’ own responses produced an average of just 3.11. The researchers caution that students may have underreported their use of AI, but say the difference nevertheless points to the limited information staff may have about how students use these tools in their studies. AI use can be difficult for lecturers to identify, particularly when they see only the final version of an assignment rather than the process through which it was produced. Students may also use AI independently of their interactions with teaching staff, leaving academics with an incomplete picture of their working practices. The research also found that students were generally more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI. Students rated the technology more highly in terms of its likely contribution to academic performance, including helping them learn about their subjects, increasing productivity and reducing workloads. They also felt more strongly than staff that appropriate conditions and support were in place to help them use AI tools. Among the uses identified in the survey, students reported using generative AI to find answers to questions and assignments, generate written work, and translate or improve the grammar of their writing. The researchers suggest that the immediate appeal of AI tools may lie in their ability to produce and improve text. However, they also argue that universities need to understand the range of ways students use the technology, rather than assume that its role in academic work is straightforward. The study also found considerable variation in staff members’ familiarity with AI. While 63 per cent of academic staff respondents had used at least one generative AI tool in the six months before the survey, some had limited practical experience of the technology. candidates.evidence_text: £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans - Prolific North Skip to content Agency musicMagpie hires Cheshire agency to help shoppers find it through search, AI and social Agency Bee Network stops get a festive makeover as two agencies team up for Christmas campaign News Manchester tech unicorn says its AI is cutting weeks of data work to hours £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 A Manchester-based fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks. READ MORE: Leeds financial tech consultancy merges with London cloud specialist In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. The funding will accelerate development of the company’s platform, support engineering and product hires, and help Crediflow serve more banks and specialist lenders. Crediflow will also extend automation across the loan lifecycle, with workflows tailored to each lender’s credit policies and processes. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs. Last year, Crediflow became one of eight companies to receive funding from PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based investment programme run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II to help scale early-stage businesses. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. Drey founded Crediflow after seeing first-hand how manual processes constrain lenders’ ability to grow. Drey Kenfack, CEO and founder of Crediflow AI, said: “Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work. “When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. candidates.lead: Cloud Imperium Games (CIG), developer of Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, brought an exclusive Squadron 42 showcase to VERSA Studios Manchester, building on its established presence in the city.
candidates.evidence_text: Cloud Imperium Games Expands VERSA Studios Partnership with Squadron 42 Showcase - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Opens in a new tab Creative & media , Digital, cyber & AI Cloud Imperium Games Expands VERSA Studios Partnership with Squadron 42 Showcase Published on November 9, 2026 News Cloud Imperium Games (CIG), developer of Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, brought an exclusive Squadron 42 showcase to VERSA Studios Manchester, building on its established presence in the city. The event was one of Manchester’s major media events of the year, bringing gamers and streamers from around the world to experience the highly anticipated game ahead of its release next year. Star Wars actor Mark Hamill, one of the game’s stars, also attended in October. VERSA supported CIG in delivering the event and co-produced the behind-the-scenes filming, including interviews with the game’s creators. More details about the filming will be shared soon. More than 40 people worked on the project, with VERSA coordinating the crew, lighting, production design, sound, studio space and other production requirements. VERSA also brought in specialist virtual production partner Mars Volume, which built the largest virtual production screen ever constructed in Manchester and created immersive content inspired by the game. A life-sized Hornet spacecraft provided by CIG was also part of the environment. Sandi Roberts, Co-Founder of Cloud Imperium Games , said: “We had a wonderful experience working with VERSA and its teams to bring our event to life.” The project showcases VERSA Studios Manchester’s capabilities across virtual production, motion capture and wider production services. Charlie Ingall, Executive Director of VERSA Studios, said: “This project shows how VERSA works as a production partner, bringing together people, technology, facilities and specialist partners across gaming, physical production and virtual production. Working with CIG, our team helped deliver an ambitious event and co-produce the behind-the-scenes filming on a feature-film scale. It’s a strong example of the scale of what can be delivered at VERSA.” CIG has an established presence at St John’s, the landmark Manchester district developed by Allied London, where it is based in the UK. It also has a permanent motion-capture studio at VERSA Studios Manchester, one of the largest of its kind in the UK. Allied London is the parent company of VERSA Media Group, which operates VERSA Studios in Manchester, Leeds and London. Events will take place at Band on the Wall, Hallé St Peter’s, Hallé at St Michael’s, The Smithfield Market Tavern, Cutting Room Square and Stoller Hall Artists announced so far include Spiers & Boden, Eliza Carthy & The Restitution, Leveret, Catrin Finch & Aoife Ní Bhriain (pictured below), Fionn Regan (pictured above), Pokey LaFarge, Olivia Chaney, Steve Knightley, Rewild: Kantos Chamber Choir x Stevens & Pound, Spencer Cullum, And it’s not just about live music. There’ll be an intriguing programme of hands-on workshops, including spoon carving, Sacred Harp singing, corn dolly making, a sound bath and drop-in sketch sessions A festival wristband will give you access to all the shows, as well as to an exclusive Jim Moray concert just for wristband holders. You’ll also be invited to the opening day celebrations with music across three stages at Stoller Hall Earlybird wristbands sold out in record time. Second-release wristbands are now on sale, with the next price increase due in late November, so secure yours now to get the best value. You can also buy individual concert tickets for headline shows

candidates.lead: Bolton Car Boot Sale at Bolton Car Boot Sale
candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Etihad Stadium Manchester City will pay extra £320k a year to the council in new Etihad Campus lease deal The town hall has shared details of its new arrangement with the Blues Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Report Manchester City will pay an extra £320,000 a year to the council for its lease at the Etihad Campus as part of an updated agreement Town hall papers published in August revealed a variation to the lease in light of the changes taking place to the stadium and surrounding land, which has been transformed into a major visitor destination since the ground first opened for the 2002 Commonwealth Games New figures released by the council have revealed it will pocket extra each year from its leases with the football club, with a further £33,000 for the stadium lease, £252,000 for City Square, and £35,680 from land in the new Medlock Square hotel and entertainment zone The extra cash will add to the total amount paid to the council by City, which stood at £6.3m last year, made up of £4.4m in rent, £1.1m from naming rights, and £790,000 from income from Champions League games Lease payments for the stadium and City Square are set to increase in future through inflation-linked increases, while the land lease at Medlock Square includes an annual rent uplift of three per cent and future reviews

candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
